title: Standardize admin API credential policy: segmentation, rotation, and audit correlation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define and implement a consistent admin API credential policy covering naming, per-scope keys, rotation cadence, expiry enforcement, and audit correlation with SSO/SAML events. This ticket drives the design and rollout for platform-admin API key hygiene used by human operators, automation jobs, and partner integrations. The policy must integrate with RBAC v2 and the new audit-log schema so every key action (create/rotate/revoke/use) is traceable to an identity (SSO principal or service identity).
acceptance_criteria: Policy document published in Confluence with examples for human and machine keys
Admin keys support: scope tags, human-readable name, creator metadata, expiry timestamp, and rotation history
Automatic enforcement: keys older than expiry are blocked and flagged in the console
Per-scope keys: keys can be limited to admin scopes (e.g., billing:read, runtime:deploy) and rejected if broader than allowed for the creator's RBAC role
Audit logs include key_id, creator_id (SSO subject), key_name, scope_list, action (create/rotate/revoke/use), and correlation_id for the request
Migration plan executed for existing long-lived admin keys: detection, notify owners, staged rotation, and revocation window
E2E tests exercising rotation, expiry enforcement, and audit correlation pass in CI
Metrics dashboard: count of expired keys, rotations/week, keys per-role, and failed auths due to expired keys
design_notes: Key model will add fields: key_name (string), key_type (human|service), scopes (list of scope strings), expires_at (ISO timestamp), rotated_from (key_id), last_used_at
We avoid a new global key store; extend existing credential table with new columns and indexes for last_used_at and expires_at

Rotation strategy: encourage short expiry (30d) for human admin keys, 90d for service keys with rotation automation. Allow exceptions via enterprise policy with explicit justification recorded in audit log

Correlate keys with SSO by requiring binding at creation or first use: if user created key while SSO session active, store sso_sub in creator_id. For programmatic onboarding (CI), require service account identity and an owner email
Reject policy: keys with wildcard scopes for admin_role_maintainers will be restricted in RBAC v2 unless a specific ACL is approved
Trade-offs: short expiries improve security but increase operational friction for customers; mitigation is rotation tooling and CLI helpers
We will emit structured audit events to Kafka with schema version 2.1 so downstream alerting and SIEM can consume
implementation_tasks: DB: add columns key_name, key_type, scopes_json, expires_at, rotated_from, last_used_at; add indexes
API: v2 endpoints for key create/rotate/revoke/list with validation of scopes against requestor's RBAC role
Console: admin credentials UI for creating keys with suggested expiry, rotation scheduler, and owner contact
CLI/SDK: helper commands for rotation and interactive key creation that integrates with SSO flow
Audit pipeline: enrich log producer to attach sso_sub and correlation_id and publish to audit topic
Migration script: scan keys without expires_at -> create migration report, email owners with rotation link
Policy engine: enforce per-role maximum scopes and default expiry via configuration
E2E tests: CI tests for create->rotate->revoke lifecycle and audit message validation
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Discovery): run job to enumerate existing admin keys and classify by age, scopes, and last_used_at; upload CSV to Confluence and S3
Phase 2 (Notify): send templated emails to key owners with rotation instructions and a 30-day deadline for keys >90d
Phase 3 (Automated Rotation Offer): enable one-click rotation for keys that support it; for pinned keys, create ticket with owner to request exception
Phase 4 (Enforcement): after deadline, automatically revoke keys that were not rotated; maintain 7-day soft-block window for critical infra with manual override
Phase 5 (Audit & Close): verify audit logs show rotation events and update PRD checklist
monitoring_and_alerting: Create Grafana dashboard with: expired_keys_count, rotations_last_30d, keys_created_by_role, failed_auths_due_to_expiry
Alert: > 5 critical (role=platform-owner) keys expired in 24h -> paged to SRE
Alert: migration revoke rate > 100/day -> stop automated revocations and notify security ops
SIEM mapping: forward audit topic to Splunk with field mapping for key_id and sso_sub
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: automated revocations could break integrations. Mitigation: staged rollout and canary policy scoped to non-prod first
Risk: owners may not be reachable. Mitigation: fallback to owner-team escalation and allow temporary emergency keys that are short-lived and require approval
Risk: audit volume increases. Mitigation: sample low-sensitivity events and provide retention tiering in audit pipeline
qa_and_testing: Unit tests for scope validation logic and RBAC checks
Integration tests for audit event emission and schema validation
Load test: bulk rotations for 50k keys to verify DB index performance
User acceptance: staged rollout with Platform team and internal SREs acting as beta users
rollout_plan: Week 1: feature-flagged backend + API on staging; internal alpha with Platform and Security
Week 2: console + CLI helpers behind flag; run migration discovery job and notify owners in dev orgs
Week 3: open beta for selected customers and Dedicated tenants; monitor metrics and gather feedback
Week 4: GA toggle on for all orgs with 30-day migration window enforced by policy; publish support KB
